title: AI Token and Cost Governance
readerIntent: Control AI quality, token consumption, quotas, and financial exposure.
priorKnowledge: Understand usage profiles and provider pricing.
owner: aiProviders token economics, persistent ledger, budgets, and operational controls
summary: Every provider call estimates, reserves, meters, records, and reconciles tokens and cost under configurable hierarchical budgets and emergency controls.

sections.heading: Optimization sequence
items: Choose the smallest capable model and operation profile.
Retrieve only permission-safe relevant evidence.
Trim duplicate or stale history and use bounded summaries.
Cache safe deterministic reusable results by complete context.
Set output limits and stop conditions.
Avoid repeated provider planning when an existing governed tool or workflow can answer deterministically.

sections.heading: Budgets and ledger
items: Configure tenant, enterprise, project, user, conversation, capability, operation, and time-window budgets as applicable.
Reserve estimated usage atomically before invocation; reject or downgrade according to explicit policy.
Record normalized input/output/cache/reasoning usage and reviewed price provenance.
Reconcile reservation with provider usage and retain a tenant-safe immutable ledger.
Expose own-usage and operator summaries through distinct permissions.

sections.heading: Worked cost-control example
items: An Axis employee asks for a summary of active modules. The assistant should call the governed registry tool and summarize its compact result instead of sending an entire module catalog to a large model.
The usage profile selects the smallest qualified model, limits retrieved evidence and output, estimates tokens, checks the employee and tenant budget, and reserves expected cost before invocation.
After completion, the gateway records provider-reported input, output, cached, and reasoning usage with the reviewed pricing version, then releases or charges the difference from the reservation.
If budget is exhausted, policy may refuse, offer a deterministic non-AI path, or use an explicitly approved cheaper model. It must never continue invisibly without accounting.

sections.heading: Fail-safe operations
items: Global and scoped kill switches, atomic request limiter, provider circuits, quotas, alerts, and bounded fallback.
No unpriced active model, silent unlimited quota, fail-open ledger, or client-selected provider.
Test concurrent budget races, retry/fallback charging, cancellation, cache hits, missing usage, price changes, outage, recovery, and reconciliation.

sections.heading: Governance evidence
items: Business owners need budgets, trend, value, and exception reports; operators need saturation, circuits, estimation variance, and reconciliation; users should see understandable limits without viewing other users' activity.
Pricing metadata is versioned because provider prices and token categories change. Unknown or stale pricing cannot silently authorize an active paid model.

Prompt and response content is not required for cost evidence. Correlation, usage dimensions, model identity, pricing provenance, decision, and safe outcome are sufficient for most operational accounting.
Regression tests confirm that caching, summaries, fallback, retries, cancellation, and streaming cannot double-charge, evade a quota, or mix usage between tenants.

sections.heading: Complete guide: How AI Cost Governance Works
paragraphs: Nodics treats AI usage limits as execution controls, not merely reports shown after money has been spent.

This page explains the implemented AI provider and persistent token-ledger foundation for business owners, administrators, and application developers. Disabled OpenAI, Anthropic, and Gemini/Vertex adapters, the backend read-only Assistant turn slice, and the documentation-focused Knowledge/RAG slice are now implemented. Browser APIs, Axis rendering, governed mutation tools, and production provider activation are later phases.

sections.heading: Why A Business Needs This
paragraphs: AI requests can vary greatly in size and price. During a busy business event, many users or automated processes may issue requests at the same time. A simple monthly report cannot prevent those concurrent requests from exceeding an approved budget.

sections.heading: Security And Accuracy
paragraphs: content.
items: Tenant and principal identity come from authenticated request context.
Provider and model come from the configured provider profile.
Pricing uses revisioned exact decimal strings.
Cost decisions never use JavaScript floating point.
Persistent data is authoritative; cache cannot approve capacity.
Generated CRUD APIs are disabled for ledger models.
Usage evidence must not contain provider credentials or sensitive prompt

Nodics now provides bounded, dry-run-first repair scans for interrupted `RECONCILING` and `RELEASING` transitions. It persists repair runs/findings, reconstructs exact counters from evidence, and accepts positive provider usage evidence for uncertain reconciliation. It never treats missing evidence as proof that usage was free.
